historical_record.description: At the Landmarks Council's request the Recreation and Park Commission approved replacing the bronze plaque on Mount Davidson honoring Madie D. Brown, whose efforts had made the summit a city park; the original plaque, put up in 1929, had been vandalized and taken.

The Board of Park Commissioners received the Supervisors' resolution placing under its charge, for park purposes, the Mount Davidson land Aug. J. Lang, Jr. had deeded to the city in two deeds, including about 7.86 acres adjoining Juanita Way.
The Board of Park Commissioners authorized its president to engage George W. Kelham as architect for the construction it planned on Mount Davidson.

The Board of Park Commissioners let the low bidder, Webster Jeffers, withdraw his $8,942 bid for building the Cross on Mount Davidson over an error in figuring the concrete, and awarded the contract to the next lowest responsible bidder, Monson Bros., for $11,850.

Because of the structural difficulties, the Board of Park Commissioners gave George W. Kelham a flat fee of $2,000 for the Mount Davidson Cross, its engineering and its floodlighting, and set aside $1,500 for about a hundred yards more concrete that the architects and engineers found its foundations needed.
